pages.text: There is no weather service in this world until you build one. The $(item)Simple Weather Alert Generator$() turns the $(l:radiocraft:sky/weather_station)weather stations$() it hears into alerts broadcast on $(thing)162.500 MHz$(), for $(l:radiocraft:sky/weather_alert_receiver)weather alert receivers$() to pick up.

pages.title: What it needs
pages.text: It hears weather stations two ways, and counts both: $(thing)APRS weather beacons$() heard by an APRS station it touches or is cabled to (an $(l:radiocraft:digital/aprs)H19$(), a $(l:radiocraft:digital/headless_tnc)Headless TNC$() or a radio computer running APRS), and $(l:radiocraft:sky/weather_observer)Weather Observers$() heard by a radio it touches, on that radio's frequency. It also needs power (1 FE/t, 12 while sending) and a VHF antenna on its coax.

pages.title: More stations, more warning
pages.text: Stations count when they are $(thing)150 blocks or more$() apart, heard in the last 30 minutes.$(br2)$(thing)One$(): warnings for what is at it now, 150 blocks round it.$(br)$(thing)Two$(): warnings for storms heading in, 5 minutes ahead.$(br)$(thing)Three or more$(): watches 15 minutes ahead and tropical statements too, for the area round them all and 200 blocks past.

pages.title: Its alerts
pages.text: With Another Weather Mod it warns of storms over its area (tornado, severe thunderstorm, hurricane, blizzard, dust storm, high wind, fog, heat, cold) and, with enough stations, of those on the way. A station reporting an inch of rain in an hour gives a flash flood warning, high wind a wind warning.

pages.title: On the air
pages.text: New alerts go out at once, the rest every minute, and with none a routine broadcast every two minutes. A radio tuned to 162.500 MHz (marine WX6) hears the data burst and, for a new warning, the 1050 Hz tone.$(br2)Right click it (or use Jade) for its status: every station it hears, how far and how long ago, and why one does not count. Two APRS stations under one callsign count once: give each its own SSID (W1ABC-1, -2...).
